questions.q: In CREATE DATABASE, what does LOG ON introduce?
options: A second filegroup for log-structured tables
The auditing log destination
A synonym for ON PRIMARY
The file spec for the transaction log, which never belongs to a filegroup
questions.explain: LOG ON introduces the transaction log's file spec. Filegroups are strictly a data-file concept — the log file is never part of any filegroup.

questions.q: What does the NAME clause in a file spec actually control?
options: The logical name SQL Server uses internally and in T-SQL, independent of the OS file name
The database's display name in SSMS
The physical path on disk
The collation of that file's contents
questions.explain: NAME is the logical name used by T-SQL commands like ALTER DATABASE ... MODIFY FILE or DBCC SHRINKFILE; FILENAME holds the physical OS path.

questions.q: What happens if you run CREATE DATABASE Reporting; with no other clauses?
options: The database is created with no data file, only a log file
The statement fails with a syntax error
SQL Server prompts interactively for file locations
SQL Server fills in file sizes and paths from the model database and instance defaults
questions.explain: Omitted clauses are filled in from the model system database and the instance's configured default data/log directories.

questions.q: Why is FILEGROWTH set as a fixed size (like 256MB) generally preferred over a percentage in production?
options: A percentage growth increment gets larger and larger as the file grows, which Lesson 23 covers as an anti-pattern
Percentage growth is not supported for data files
There is no difference in behavior between the two
Fixed-size growth is required by SQL Server for log files
questions.explain: Percentage-based growth compounds: on a very large file, each growth event allocates enormous, unpredictable amounts. Fixed-size growth is predictable.

questions.q: What does MAXSIZE control in a file spec, and what happens if it's omitted?
options: It disables autogrowth entirely
It determines the file's physical block size
It sets the file's initial size
It caps how large autogrowth can take the file; if omitted, growth defaults to UNLIMITED
questions.explain: MAXSIZE is a ceiling on autogrowth. Leaving it off means the file can grow without a defined limit (UNLIMITED), constrained only by available disk space.
